_readme: THIS FILE IS HAND-EDITED. Everything the promo site says lives here — copy, links, which
screenshots appear, how many feed items each panel shows. Edit it, commit, done.
site/feeds.json is the OTHER file, and it is generated by tools/site-feeds.mjs. Never edit
that one: a scheduled refresh overwrites it. The split is deliberate, so an automated feed
pull can never clobber the words on the page.
To point the CTA at a real Steam page, set cta.steam.url and the button stops saying soon.
site.url is used for metadata only. The og: tags in index.html hold the SAME url and are
the one place it is duplicated — link scrapers do not run JS, so they cannot read it from
here. If the site moves, change both.

site.title: WHALE HOP — Lassen Seas
site.description: A time-trial of flips, momentum and moonlight. Climb from the abyssal trench to the top of the sky.
site.author: el3v8or

game.name: WHALE HOP
game.subtitle: LASSEN SEAS
game.tagline: a time-trial of flips, momentum & moonlight
game.blurb: You are a whale with somewhere to be. Breach, flip, grind a rail to its end, and turn the momentum into altitude — from the floor of the abyssal trench, through a sunset, past a ringed planet, and out the top of the sky.
pitch: Every run is a climb. Speed is the only currency, and tricks are how you mint it.
Nineteen named bands stack from −3,600m to 700,000m, and each one looks like nowhere else in the game.
One file, no installer, no launcher, sixty ticks a second of deterministic simulation.

steam.label: WISHLIST ON STEAM
steam.note: Steam page not up yet. Follow along on Bluesky for the announcement.

features.title: Glyphs for the world, vector art for the things in it
features.body: The sky, the sea, the starfield and the seafloor are drawn from monospace characters — a hundred thousand points of drifting texture. Anything you have to recognise at speed is a vector: the whale, the fish, the bumpers, the satellites. Both layers share one near-black outline, which is what stops it looking like sprites pasted on a text screen.

features.title: Nineteen bands, and the sky is a journey
features.body: Sunrise gold at the waterline, a pink band at 900m, violet at 2,600, deep indigo, near-black, and then space. It should never be flat until THE ARCADE at 300,000m, where black is the point and six saturated colours are deliberately louder than anything below.

features.title: Screen-wide effects are for rare events
features.body: Collect something and sparks come off the hull, coloured by what you took and thrown backward along your flight. Tier up the heat and you get a shockwave, not a flash. The full-screen flash has exactly seven triggers, all of them rare, and adding an eighth needs a reason.

features.title: An endless hub, and authored levels with medals
features.body: DIVE gives you the endless climb. The levels are compositions with their own sky, their own sea and their own objectives — a hydrothermal plume followed from a black-smoker field to ice at the edge of space, or a sugar boil that breaks the surface as fizz. Bronze is the floor: finishing is the achievement, and the tiers are how well.

shots.caption: An authored level at its waterline, with its own sky gradient and its own sea. Objective: reach 10,000m.
The pink band — and a school that keeps following you as long as you keep it together.
Violet, and the last altitude where the sky still has weather in it.
Above the weather. The height map down the left edge is the only thing that still says which way is up.
Backdrop bodies are placed, not scattered — the ringed planet never appears below 15,000m.
Where the sky turns a faint purple and the void blobs start eating the starfield.
Six saturated colours on pure black, deliberately louder than anything below it. The bumpers were chosen by hand, not derived.
